data.text:
All seven scenarios hold, so I wrote `{"findings": []}` to `findings.json`. I judged this by reading the code and tests; I didn't run any tests, as the rules require.

- **Awaited dependencies** (`src/core/spec/stack-dependencies.ts`): an overlap line whose change now has a different hash is kept and marked `reapproved: true` instead of being dropped. `tests/approve-overlap.test.ts` covers all five rows of the table. The base code dropped that line, so the updated test would fail on the base.
- **Stacked cut** (`src/core/spec/stack-cut.ts`): an overlap line is now skipped only when its change is unapproved, so a re-approved change makes the stacked change wait. In `tests/stack-overlap-cut.test.ts`, the re-approved row now expects `{ kind: 'wait' }`, no regression marker and no branch; the other rows were already covered.
- **Re-approved before it lands**: `tests/stack-overlap-reapproved.test.ts` runs the whole sequence. After the first cycle no `osq/002-b` branch exists, the stacked approval is still there and there's no regression marker. Once `001-a` is archived and squash-merged into `main`, the next cycle cuts `osq/002-b` from `main`. On the base it would have cut on the first cycle, so the test would fail there.
- **Inbox** (`src/core/status/inbox-overlap.ts`, plus changes to `inbox-projection.ts` and `inbox-text.ts`): the new `overlap-reapproved` item and its text line are tested in `tests/inbox-overlap-reapproved.test.ts`. It goes through all three rows and checks `readInbox`, the `--json` output and the text inbox. The base had no such item kind.
- **Show** (`show-runs-after.ts`, `show-types.ts`): `tests/show-runs-reapproved.test.ts` checks the exact `Runs after: … approved again since` line right after `Depends on:`, and the `runsAfter` JSON.
- **Web**: the new label in `labels.ts` and the `; approved again since` suffix in `ChangeHeader.tsx` each have a test that would fail on the base. The web data's `runsAfter` type comes from the show types, so it carries `reapproved` too.

Most of the patch (Rust approve/retry code and fixtures) comes from the main-branch sync and isn't part of these scenarios, so I didn't judge it.
